newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares gain, fuelled by BTC.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares gain, fuelled by BTC.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose 0.62 percent on Wednesday, largely boosted by strong demand for the shares of warehouse operator BTC, traders said.
The SBI index climbed 8.38 points to 1,350.57 but volume remained low, reflecting the continued absence of foreign investors, traders said.
"Our market depends on accessibility -- unless it opens up to foreign capital no major changes can be expected in the near future," said Andrej Ciuha, a trader at brokerage Inter Timex.
Overall eight shares rose and seven fell, one was flat and 11 were untraded. Turnover slipped to 92.8 million tolars from 93.2 million.

Foreign investment was blocked in February by the central bank ordering foreign portfolio investors to open custody accounts at one of Slovenia's fully licensed banks in order to be able to trade in the country's securities.
Finance Minister Mitja Gaspari criticised the costs of foreign custody accounts by saying that such high costs are hampering the international competitiveness of local banks.

BTC was the most actively traded share and the top gainer, firming 1.8 percent to 14,559 tolars on volume of 1,556 shares. This week alone BTC has surged 10.6 percent on rumours it was planning to issue global depository receipts within the next six months.
BTC said it was seeking fresh capital, but added issuing GDRs was only one of the options they were considering.
Brokerage Dadas led the day's decliners, falling 4.58 percent to 7,500 tolars on volume of three shares.
